JUDGMENT

This is a petition filed u/s. 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act and Rule 232 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules claiming for compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.

2. The petitioner's case in brief as follows:
On 30-10-2021 at about 5.30 p.m. when the petitioner was walking on the extreme left side of the road near MES ring road at Kuvempu circle underpass and was moving towards Gorguntepalya ring road, at that time, driver of the lorry bearing reg.No.KA-08-8808 came from opposite direction with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, violating traffic rules and regulations, lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the petitioner, due to which petitioner sustained severe injuries and took treatment at M.S.Ramaiah hospital, Bangalore as inpatient from 30-10-2021 to 29-11- 2021 and underwent surgery and petitioner took treatment at NIMHANS hospital, Bangalore as inpatient from 1-1-2021 to 15-12-2021 and spent money for treatment.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.25 lakhs from the respondents.
3. In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.1 and 2 appeared through their respective counsel and only respondent No.1 filed written statement.

4. Respondent No.1 filed written statement wherein contended that they have not issued a policy of insurance in respect of the lorry bearing No.KA-08-8808 in question in favour of 2nd respondent on the date of accident.
They have issued policy in respondent of lorry which is valid from 6-12- 2021 to 5-12-2022 i.e., insurance policy obtained after 36 days of the alleged accident.
There is no privity of contract between insurance company and 2nd respondent for any sort of indemnification.
This respondent is not necessary and proper party for the adjudication of the above petition.
Hence prays to dismiss the above claim petition with cost.
5. From the above said pleadings three issues are framed:

sentences.text: 1. Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing reg.No.KA-08-8808 on 30-10-2021 at about 5.30 p.m. near MES ring road at Kuvempu circle underpass, Bengaluru city ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
6.
The petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and Exs.P1 to P13 documents are marked.
On the other hand, respondents have not led their defence evidence.

7. Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
8.

My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1:

In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, the petitioner examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 13 documents as Ex-P1 to 13 i.e.,FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, rough sketch, wound certificate, charge sheet, discharge summaries, inpatient bills, medical bills, IMV report, aadhaar card.
10. The respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel and not at all denied the involvement of the vehicle, cause and manner of the accident and in generally denied the entire claim petition.
The respondent No.1 only taken the contention that as on the date of the accident, they have not issued the policy and hence there is no contract between them and 2 nd respondent.

But during the cross-examination of the PW-1 learned counsel for the respondent No.1 cross examined PW-1 at length and suggested as petitioner was crossing the road other than the underpass road and hence the accident had been taken place which has been entirely denied by the PW-1.

Further it was suggested that there was no signal and footpath road and zebra cross on the road in which the petitioner was crossing the road and hence accident had been taken place, but the said suggestion has been categorically denied by the PW-1.
PW-1 categorically stated that at the time of accident, she was going on the foot path road and she was not crossing the road.
Further PW-1 stated that at the time of accident, she was moving from Goraguntepalya towards Hebbal.

Further it was suggested by the counsel for the respondent No.1 that there was barricades on both sides of the road at the spot of accident for which PW-1 stated that accident had been taken place not at the place where barricades Aishwarya K.K vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160924435/
3 were placed, but accident had been taken place after the barricades are place.

entities.text: Aishwarya K.K vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: PW-1 further stated that after the barricades there is a service road and after the service road there is a foot path and accident has been taken place in the foot path.

In this regard, on perusal of the sketch Ex-P4 it clearly shows that accident has been taken place at the extreme left edge of the road where there is a foot path and left side of the road from Goraguntepalya towards Hebbal.
On perusal of Ex-P3 sketch and Ex-P4 it clearly shows that driver of the Tipper lorry has drove the lorry towards the extreme left side of the road.
Ex-P3 and 4 demonstrate that the accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the Tipper lorry.

Though respondent No.1 insurance company has denied the cause and manner of the accident, but has not examined the driver of the lorry who is an important and material eye witness to say as to state about the facts and circumstances of the case.
The non examination of the driver of the lorry is fatal to the case of the respondent No.1.
Thus respondent No.1 has failed to prove the contention taken by him.

11. Moreover the evidence and materials on record reveals that soon after the accident, one K.K.Aishwarya has lodged the complaint and thereafter the jurisdictional police have conducted the thorough and detailed investigation against the driver of the Tipper lorry.

On 30-1-2021 at about 6.30 p.m. accused drove the lorry bearing No.KA-08-8808 from Goraguntepalya towards Hebbal in high speed and in rash and negligent manner near MES ring road near Kuvempu circle and hit to the petitioner who was pedestrian moving on the same road at the extreme left side of the road, as a result of which petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly concerned jurisdictional police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the lorry for the offences punishable U/s 279, 338 of I.P.C.
12.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Ex.P12 IMV report indicates that the occurrence of the said accident was not due to any of the mechanical defects of the vehicle involved in the accident.

13. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
14. Thus, the oral evidence of PW-1 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text:
With this observation issue No.1 in is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
16. ISSUE NO.2:
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
17. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME:
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident she was aged 44 years.
From the Ex-P13- Aadhaar card it reveals that petitioner's date of birth is 19- 10-1978.

Hence as on the date of accident i.e.,2021,
petitioner was aged about 43 years.
The petitioner has stated that she was doing Tailoring work and earning Rs.15,000/- per month and due to accidental injuries, she is suffering from permanent disability and deformity.
The petitioner has not produced any document regarding his avocation and income.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of his work, if his income is assessed at Rs.15,000/- p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.

18. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:-
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove hER disability.
Therefore this tribunal is not awarding compensation under the head loss of future income due to disability.

19. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
As per the Ex-P5-wound certificate the petitioner has sustained injuries (1) a boggy swelling over left supra orbital area (2) an avulsed lacerated wound of 4 x 3 cm on upper lip (3) a lacerated wound 3 x 0.5 cm with abrasion around the wound on right elbow (4) internal degloving injury over right thigh, knee and leg, chemosis present and above said injuries are simple in nature.
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner being 43 years and certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.

20. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and took treatment at M.S.Ramaiah memorial hospital as inpatient from 30-10-2021 to 10-11-2021 and from 10-11-2021 to 29-11-2021.

Further petitioner took treatment as inpatient at NIMHANS hospital, Bangalore from 01-12-2021 to 15-12-2021 total for a period of 45 days and it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out her avocation Aishwarya K.K vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160924435/
5 for at least 4 months.

entities.text: Aishwarya K.K vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.60,000/- (15,000 X 4) under the head loss of income during the laid up period.
21. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner is a resident of Gokula,
Bangalore and has taken treatment as inpatient at M.S.Ramaiah memorial hospital as inpatient from 30-10-2021 to 10-11-2021 and from 10-11- 2021 to 29-11-2021.

Further petitioner took treatment as inpatient at NIMHANS hospital, Bangalore from 01-12-2021 to 15-12-2021 for 45 days as inpatient and certainly she would have hired the cab for traveling to the hospital and underwent primary suturing of upper lip laceration and debridement and drainage of hematoma right lower limb under GA on 31-10- 2021, wound debridement, SSG to wound right leg and suturing of right leg wound under SA on 5-11-2021.

Upper lip laceration repair+drainage of hematoma of right leg on 31-10- 2021 and SSG over wound in right lower limb on 3-11-2021 and certainly, it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of her treatment the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.

Hence a sum of Rs.55,000/-
under this head.

22. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The petitioner doing work of tailoring, certainly injuries sustained by her in accident will cause the disability.
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.35,000/- is awarded under this head.
23. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced Ex-P9,10-inpatient bills and Ex-P11-medical bills for Rs.4,61,199/- to prove the expenditure towards treatment taken by her.

From the said medical bills amount, NIMHANS hospital bill amount of Rs.14,312=28 is deducted (Rs.4,61,199/- - Rs.14,312=28)= Rs.4,46,886=72, as it relates to treatment taken by PW-1 with regard to her earlier disability and injury not caused due to accident.
Hence petitioner is entitle for total medical bill of Rs.4,46,886=72.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident,
the resultant disability suffered by her due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.4,46,886=72 under the head of medical expenses.

24. The calculation table stands as follows :

INTEREST & LIABILITY:

The counsel for the respondent No.1 disputed that they have not issued the insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle in favour of the respondent No.2 as on the date of the accident and contended that they have issued the policy in respect of 2 nd respondent which was valid and effective from 6-12-2021 to 5- 12-2022 where as the alleged accident have taken place on 30-10-2021 i.e., insurance policy obtained after 36 days of the alleged accident and hence they are not liable to pay the compensation.

On the other hand, petitioner has produced copy of the insurance policy and policy summary down loaded from the internet as per Ex-P14 and also produced 65B certificate as per Ex-P15 in support of Ex-P14.

As per Ex-P14, respondent No.1 has issued the policy to the offending vehicle on 25-11-2020 and it was valid from 25-11-2020 to 24-11- 2021 and alleged date of accident is 30-10-2021 i.e.,
accident had been taken place within the period of insurance.
Hence, it is clear from Ex-P14 that as on the date of accident, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1 in respect of the respondent o.2 was valid.

Moreover, it is pertinent to note here that counsel for the respondent No.1 has not at all disputed Ex-P14 document and also with regard to the validity of the policy in the cross-examination of the PW-1 by putting single suggestion.
Hence, it appears that for the sake of defence only respondent No.1 has taken the said contention.
26. Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
27. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.1 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
28. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :

sentences.text: The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,96,886=72 with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 is hereby directed to deposit total compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, 40% shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in open court on this the 10th day of March 2025).

Bengaluru.
